note: Mississippi sets the highest bar of any state here for complaining about a clinician: the complaint must be written, signed under oath and notarised, on the Board's own form, and it must name the specific statute or rule you say was broken and the dates of what happened. Anonymous complaints are not investigated at all. Worth preparing properly rather than sending something that will be returned.

civil_injury.summary: Only one year from the injury for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Negligence and other personal injury claims have three years.
civil_injury.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-35; Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-49
civil_injury.quote: All actions for assault, assault and battery, maiming, false imprisonment, malicious arrest, or menace, and all actions for slanderous words concerning the person or title, for failure to employ, and for libels, shall be commenced within one (1) year next after the cause of such action accrued, and not after.
civil_injury.note: § 15-1-49(1): 'All actions for which no other period of limitation is prescribed shall be commenced within three (3) years next after the cause of such action accrued' (https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-15/chapter-1/section-15-1-49/), with a discovery rule for latent injury (§ 15-1-49(2)). Read on Justia's 2025 Mississippi Code (the official code is published by LexisNexis); 2026 session changes not checked.

civil_minor_tolling.summary: The clock does not start until the injured person is no longer a minor, and in Mississippi a minor is anyone under 21 for this purpose. So an assault or battery claim can be brought until the 22nd birthday, and a negligence claim until the 24th. There is no longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.
civil_minor_tolling.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-59; Miss. Code Ann. § 1-3-27
civil_minor_tolling.quote: If any person entitled to bring any of the personal actions mentioned shall, at the time at which the cause of action accrued, be under the disability of infancy or unsoundness of mind, he may bring the actions within the times in this chapter respectively limited, after his disability shall be removed as provided by law.
civil_minor_tolling.note: Age 21 comes from § 1-3-27: 'minor' includes 'any person ... under twenty-one (21) years of age' except for contracts (https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-1/chapter-3/section-1-3-27/). That § 15-1-59's 'disability of infancy' ends at 21 rather than 18 is the reading of § 1-3-27 but was not confirmed against case law. No cap on the infancy saving appears in § 15-1-59.

civil_government_claims.summary: Under the Mississippi Tort Claims Act, suit must be filed within one year of the conduct, and a written notice of claim must be served on the government's chief executive officer at least 90 days before suing; minors get the year after their disability ends.
civil_government_claims.quote: All actions brought under this chapter shall be commenced within one (1) year next after the date of the tortious, wrongful or otherwise actionable conduct on which the liability phase of the action is based, and not after, except that filing a notice of claim within the required one-year period will toll the statute of limitations for ninety-five (95) days
civil_government_claims.note: § 11-46-11(1): 'at least ninety (90) days before instituting suit, the person must file a notice of claim with the chief executive officer of the governmental entity.' § 11-46-11(4) preserves the infancy saving. The MTCA excludes some intentional conduct from government liability (§ 11-46-5, -7, not read).

criminal_child_abuse.summary: No time limit for felonious abuse or battery of a child. Misdemeanor child abuse or neglect must be charged within two years.
criminal_child_abuse.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 99-1-5(1)(a); Miss. Code Ann. § 97-5-39(2)
criminal_child_abuse.quote: The passage of time shall never bar prosecution against any person for the offenses of murder, manslaughter, aggravated assault, aggravated domestic violence, kidnapping, ... felonious abuse or battery of a child as described in Section 97-5-39
criminal_child_abuse.note: Felonious child abuse (§ 97-5-39(2)) includes burning, choking or interfering with breathing, starving, and whipping or striking a child where serious bodily harm occurs. Other offenses, including misdemeanor abuse or neglect under § 97-5-39(1), have two years (§ 99-1-5(2)). § 99-1-5 was last amended by Laws 2024, ch. 519 (Justia 2025 edition).

criminal_felony_assault.summary: No time limit for aggravated assault. Simple assault and other offenses not listed: two years.
criminal_felony_assault.quote: (2) A person shall not be prosecuted for any other offense not listed in this section unless the prosecution for the offense is commenced within two (2) years after the commission thereof.
criminal_felony_assault.note: Aggravated assault is in the no-limit list of § 99-1-5(1)(a) (quoted under criminal_child_abuse). The limit does not run while the accused has fled or is absent from the state (§ 99-1-5(3)).

channels.name: Mississippi Board of Examiners for Social Workers and Marriage and Family Therapists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines social workers and marriage and family therapists in Mississippi, and publishes its disciplinary actions. Any person, firm, corporation, board member or public officer may complain.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It will not investigate an anonymous complaint, and it will only formally address one that arrives in writing on its form.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed social worker or marriage and family therapist in Mississippi.
channels.how: Use the Board's official complaint form. It must be in writing, signed under oath and notarised, must specify the statute or rule allegedly violated, and must set out the acts or omissions and the dates they happened. Post the completed notarised form to the Board.

channels.name: Mississippi Child Abuse Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour report line run by the Department of Child Protection Services, for abuse, neglect, exploitation and human trafficking. Staff of residential care facilities and group homes licensed by the Department count as persons responsible for the care of children, so their conduct falls squarely within what this line takes.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Mississippi program.
channels.how: Call the hotline, or report online through the Department's site.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

channels.name: Mississippi State Department of Health, Child Care Facilities Licensure
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses child care facilities in Mississippi and runs a dedicated licensure complaint line, separate from the child abuse hotline.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed facility, where the issue is a licensing breach rather than abuse.
channels.phone_note: Child Care Facilities Licensure complaint line, toll free.

channels.name: Disability Rights Mississippi
channels.what_it_can_do: Mississippi's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Mississippi program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
